text:
Eleni: Heads-up: noticed a regression in nightly where smallpage churn increased by ~3x after the allocator refactor. this correlates with more frequent host-offloads during steady state.
Marco: I dug a bit: allocator now uses finer-grained slabs which reduced internal fragmentation but exposed many short-lived tiny allocations that get pinned then offloaded.
Priya: right 12 these tiny allocations make offload work harder; eviction granularity is page-aligned so we end up moving many small objects leading to write amplification.
Theo: options: (A) batch tiny allocs into a small-object arena to make residency decisions coarser, (B) change offload unit to sub-page logical objects with scatter/gather DMA (complex), (C) add a tiny-allocation cooldown to avoid immediate offload.
Eleni: tradeoffs: (A) reduces DMA ops but increases allocator complexity and may reintroduce internal fragmentation. (B) fast but requires DMA engine and PCIe scatter support and big refactor. (C) simplest but may increase peak memory usage.
Marco: benchmark idea: simulate steady allocation pattern with 100k tiny allocations/sec and measure dma_ops, pcie_util, and spill_bytes for each option.
Priya: also need to consider fairness: coalescing may group objects from multiple tenants on same slab -> leakage/risk. must retain tenant-aware segregation or tags.
Theo: suggestion: small-object arena per-tenant-per-numa. keep per-tenant accounting and eviction tags. that keeps isolation while allowing coalescing.
Eleni: what about fragmentation long-term? If we batch tiny allocs into arena, we'll need periodic compaction to reclaim freed holes. compaction itself can be paused or rate-limited.
Marco: compaction policy: background async compaction with residency-friendly windows; avoid compaction during high tail-latency periods. add backpressure from latency SLO metrics.
Priya: metadata cost: arena headers and compaction maps add memory; but overall should be net-win vs DMA waste. need telemetry: small_alloc_churn, arena_coalesce_hits, compaction_io_bytes.
Theo: for immediate mitigation, I can add a short holdback_ms (default 50ms) for tiny allocations: delay offload decisions to see if object is released soon. low-risk and fast to ship behind flag.
Eleni: good short-term. longer-term RFC: per-tenant small-object arenas + compaction + tenant-aware coalescing. include invariants: no cross-tenant mixing, TTL for arenas, and max_arena_size to bound waste.
Priya: sample quick config:
```
small_alloc:
  tiny_threshold_bytes: 256
  holdback_ms: 50
  arena:
    enabled: true
    max_arena_size_mb: 64
    per_tenant: true
    compaction_rate_mb_per_s: 4
    compaction_backoff_tail_ms: 200
```
ci-bot: canary: deploying holdback_ms=50 to stg-offload-1 at 03:00 UTC; auto-rollback if spill_bytes increases > 1.5x for 10m.
Marco: dev tasks: (1) implement holdback path in residency policy, (2) prototype per-tenant arena allocator, (3) compaction job with SLO-aware backoff.
Eleni: risks: subtle correctness around pin/unpin during compaction. mitigation: strong tests + simulation harness.
Priya: ok I'll draft RFC outline and include microbench results for holdback.
Theo: ping me for arena API review.
Eleni: thanks everyone. follow-up meeting next Tue if canary looks good. :sparkles:
